reasons.1: slugify replaces each non-alphanumeric character with a hyphen individually, without collapsing runs or stripping leading/trailing hyphens. The docstring promises single hyphens per run and no leading/trailing hyphen, so the code does not match its spec.
reasons.2: Docstring says shares sum to exactly cents and the first shares get the extra cent; split_amount(1000,3) returns [333,333,333], summing to 999. The code ignores the remainder, so it violates the spec. Bug.
reasons.3: word_count splits on whitespace, and the docstring says punctuation stays attached and "don't" is one word. "don't stop" gives 2 words, matching the docstring. The reporter wants contraction expansion, which the docstring does not promise.
reasons.4: add_business_days adds calendar days then skips weekends/holidays without counting days. Thursday+3 calendar = Sunday, skipped to Monday 11-09. Docstring says the result is `days` business days after start, but the code never decrements per business day, so it's wrong: should be Tuesday 11-10. Bug.
reasons.5: merge_intervals does not sort its input, yet the docstring promises the result is sorted by start time and accepts intervals in any order. For [[8,10],[1,3],[2,6]] it returns [[8,10],[1,6]], which is unsorted and leaves overlapping-free but misordered output. This contradicts the docstring, so it is a bug.
reasons.6: Docstring says up to and including 1 kg is $5.00 (500 cents). Code uses `if weight_kg < 1` so weight 1 falls through to the <=5 branch and returns 900. Code contradicts docstring: bug.
reasons.7: The issue requests a new feature: free shipping over $50. shipping_cost's docstring defines weight-based pricing only and makes no promise about order totals. Nothing in the docstring is violated, so this is a feature request.
reasons.8: median returns ordered[len//2] without averaging for even counts. Docstring says even count gives average of two middle values, e.g. median([4,1,3,2]) == 2.5. For [10,20,30,40] it returns 30, not 25. Code contradicts docstring.
reasons.9: Docstring says over 5 kg is the heavy tier, up to and including 5 kg is $9.00. shipping_cost(5) returns 900 via weight_kg <= 5, matching the spec. The reporter wants a different tier boundary, which is a behavior change, not a bug.
reasons.10: The docstring says the result is at most limit characters including "...", and words are not cut mid-word. The code returns text[:limit] + "...", which is 33 chars for limit 30 and cuts mid-word. This contradicts the spec, so it is a bug.

results.title: Slugs have double hyphens and a hyphen at the end

fix.new_code:
"""Text helpers for product pages."""

import unicodedata


def slugify(title):
    """Turn a product title into a URL slug.

    The slug is lowercase ASCII. Accented letters lose their accents (é becomes e). Letters and
    digits are kept. Every run of other characters (spaces, punctuation, symbols) becomes a single
    hyphen, and the slug never starts or ends with a hyphen. A title with no letters or digits gives
    the empty string.

        slugify("Wireless Headphones") == "wireless-headphones"
        slugify("USB-C Dock (2nd gen)") == "usb-c-dock-2nd-gen"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Mug") == "creme-brulee-mug"
    """
    # Decompose accented characters and drop the combining marks, leaving plain ASCII.
    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title.lower())
    ascii_text = normalized.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")

    out = []
    pending_hyphen = False
    for ch in ascii_text:
        if ch.isalnum():
            if pending_hyphen and out:
                out.append("-")
            pending_hyphen = False
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            pending_hyphen = True
    return "".join(out)


def word_count(text):
    """Count the words in a review.

    Words are separated by whitespace. Punctuation stays attached to the word it touches, so
    "great," and "don't" are one word each.

        word_count("Great keyboard, fast shipping") == 4
    """
    return len(text.split())
fix.note: slugify replaced each non-alphanumeric character with its own hyphen, so runs produced double hyphens and trailing hyphens survived. I rewrote it to emit a single hyphen per run of separators and only between alphanumerics, which also strips leading/trailing hyphens. I also added NFKD accent stripping so accented letters become ASCII as the docstring promises.

results.title: Shared payment loses a cent

fix.new_code:
"""Payments."""


def split_amount(cents, people):
    """Split an amount in cents into `people` shares, for a shared order.

    The shares add up to exactly `cents` and differ by at most one cent. When the amount does not
    divide evenly, the first shares get the extra cent. A negative amount (a refund) is split the
    same way as the positive amount, with every share negative. `people` is at least 1.

        split_amount(900, 3) == [300, 300, 300]
        split_amount(1000, 3) == [334, 333, 333]
        split_amount(-1000, 3) == [-334, -333, -333]
    """
    sign = -1 if cents < 0 else 1
    base, extra = divmod(abs(cents), people)
    return [sign * (base + 1 if i < extra else base) for i in range(people)]

results.title: Delivery date skips over the weekend wrong

fix.new_code:
"""Order and delivery dates."""
from datetime import timedelta


def add_business_days(start, days, holidays=()):
    """The date `days` business days after `start`.

    Business days are Monday to Friday, except the dates in `holidays`. Saturdays, Sundays, and
    holidays are skipped. `days` is zero or more. With days == 0 the result is `start` itself, even
    if `start` is not a business day. Otherwise the result is always a business day.

        # 2026-11-06 is a Friday
        add_business_days(date(2026, 11, 6), 1) == date(2026, 11, 9)                             # Monday
        add_business_days(date(2026, 11, 6), 1, holidays={date(2026, 11, 9)}) == date(2026, 11, 10)
    """
    if days == 0:
        return start
    result = start
    remaining = days
    while remaining > 0:
        result += timedelta(days=1)
        if result.weekday() < 5 and result not in holidays:
            remaining -= 1
    return result
fix.note: add_business_days added calendar days and then skipped weekends/holidays without counting business days, so Thu 2026-11-05 + 3 gave Mon 11-09 instead of Tue 11-10. I changed it to step one day at a time and decrement the remaining count only on Monday-Friday non-holiday dates; days == 0 still returns start unchanged.

results.title: Delivery windows overlap after merging

fix.new_code:
"""Delivery time windows."""


def merge_intervals(intervals):
    """Merge overlapping delivery windows.

    `intervals` is a list of [start, end] pairs with start <= end, in any order. Windows that
    overlap or touch (one ends where the next starts) are merged into one. The result is sorted by
    start time.

    Returns a new list. The input list and the pairs in it are not modified.

        merge_intervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10]]) == [[1, 6], [8, 10]]
        merge_intervals([[1, 4], [4, 5]]) == [[1, 5]]
    """
    merged = []
    for start, end in sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: iv[0]):
        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])
    return merged
fix.note: merge_intervals did not sort its input, so unordered windows were merged against the wrong neighbour and the output came out misordered (e.g. [[8,10],[1,3],[2,6]] gave [[8,10],[1,6]]). I now iterate over sorted(intervals, key=start), which yields the sorted, merged result; new lists are still created so the input is not mutated.

fix.new_code:
"""Shipping prices."""
import math


def shipping_cost(weight_kg):
    """The shipping price of a package, in cents.

    - Up to and including 1 kg: $5.00
    - Over 1 kg, up to and including 5 kg: $9.00
    - Over 5 kg: $9.00 plus $2.00 for each started kilogram over 5

        shipping_cost(0.4) == 500
        shipping_cost(5.2) == 1100
    """
    if weight_kg <= 1:
        return 500
    if weight_kg <= 5:
        return 900
    return 900 + 200 * math.ceil(weight_kg - 5)

"""Statistics for the sales dashboard."""


def median(values):
    """The median of a non-empty list of numbers.

    The values can be in any order, and the list is not modified. With an odd number of values the
    median is the middle one. With an even number it is the average of the two middle values.

        median([3, 1, 2]) == 2

    ordered = sorted(values)

results.title: Product card description runs past the edge of the card

fix.new_code:
"""Product cards on the store's listing pages."""


def truncate(text, limit):
    """Shorten a product description so that it fits on a product card.

    If `text` is at most `limit` characters long, it is returned unchanged. Otherwise the result
    ends with "..." and is at most `limit` characters long, the "..." included. Words are never cut
    in the middle: the result keeps as many whole words from the start as fit, separated by single
    spaces, with no space before the "...". If not even the first word fits, the result is the first
    `limit - 3` characters followed by "...". `limit` is at least 10.

        truncate("Wireless headphones", 30) == "Wireless headphones"
        truncate("Wireless noise-cancelling headphones with case", 30) == "Wireless noise-cancelling..."
    """
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    budget = limit - 3
    kept = ""
    for word in text.split():
        candidate = word if not kept else kept + " " + word
        if len(candidate) > budget:
            break
        kept = candidate
    if kept:
        return kept + "..."
    return text[:budget] + "..."
fix.note: truncate sliced text[:limit] and appended "...", giving limit+3 characters and cutting words mid-word. It now keeps whole words within limit-3 characters (joined by single spaces) before adding "...", and falls back to text[:limit-3] + "..." only when the first word doesn't fit. The headphones example now returns "Wireless noise-cancelling..." (28 chars).

baseline.report:
# huskyutils: open issue triage

All 25 existing tests pass after the changes (`cd /home/daytona/repo && python -m unittest discover -s tests`).
Tests and docstrings were not modified. Each fix follows the docstring, which the README names as the spec.

## Issue #1: Slugs have double hyphens and a hyphen at the end
- **Decision:** bug.
- **Changed:** `huskyutils/text.py`, `slugify`. Non-ASCII letters are now decomposed (NFKD) and accents
  dropped, so "é" becomes "e". Only ASCII letters and digits are kept. Each run of other characters
  becomes one hyphen, and leading or trailing hyphens are stripped. Added `import unicodedata`.
- **Checked:** `slugify("Hello, World! T-shirt")` gives `hello-world-t-shirt`, `slugify("Webcam (HD)")`
  gives `webcam-hd`, `"Crème Brûlée Mug"` gives `creme-brulee-mug`, and `"!!!"` gives `""`.

## Issue #2: Shared payment loses a cent
- **Decision:** bug. The docstring says the shares sum to exactly `cents` and that the first shares get
  the extra cent. The reporter's suggestion (extra cent to the last person) contradicts the docstring,
  so I followed the docstring. If the team wants the last person to pay the extra cent, the docstring
  must change first.
- **Changed:** `huskyutils/money.py`, `split_amount`. Positive amounts use `divmod`, giving `extra` shares
  of `base + 1` followed by the rest of `base`. Negative amounts are split as their absolute value and
  then negated. This also fixed a second bug: `split_amount(-1000, 3)` returned three -334s, which
  summed to -1002.
- **Checked:** `split_amount(1000, 3) == [334, 333, 333]`; `split_amount(-1000, 3) == [-334, -333, -333]`
  (sum -1000); `split_amount(1, 3) == [1, 0, 0]`; `split_amount(900, 3) == [300, 300, 300]`.

## Issue #3: word_count says "don't stop" is 2 words
- **Decision:** not_a_bug. The docstring says words are split on whitespace and that punctuation,
  including the apostrophe in "don't", stays attached, so "don't" is one word. The code does this.
  The word count is correct for the stated rule. If the review limit should count "don't" as two words,
  that is a spec change and would need a new docstring.
- **Changed:** nothing.
- **Checked:** `word_count("don't stop") == 2`, consistent with the docstring.

## Issue #4: Delivery date skips over the weekend wrong
- **Decision:** bug. The code added the calendar days first and then moved forward past weekends. That
  made the result wrong whenever a weekend was crossed.
- **Changed:** `huskyutils/dates.py`, `add_business_days`. The function now steps one day at a time
  and counts only days that are Monday to Friday and not in `holidays`. `days == 0` still returns `start`.
- **Checked:** `add_business_days(date(2026,11,5), 3) == date(2026,11,10)`. The existing Friday+1 and
  holiday tests still pass. Friday+1 with a Monday holiday gives Tuesday, and zero days returns the start date.

## Issue #5: Delivery windows overlap after merging
- **Decision:** bug. The docstring says the input may be in any order, but the code assumed it was sorted.
- **Changed:** `huskyutils/intervals.py`, `merge_intervals`. The loop now runs over `sorted(intervals)`.
  This does not modify the input, and the output lists are still new.
- **Checked:** `merge_intervals([[8,10],[1,3],[2,6]]) == [[1,6],[8,10]]`. Touching windows still merge:
  `[[1,4],[4,5]]` gives `[[1,5]]`.

## Issue #6: A 1 kg package is charged $9 shipping
- **Decision:** bug. The docstring says "Up to and including 1 kg: $5.00", but the code used `< 1`.
- **Changed:** `huskyutils/shipping.py`, `shipping_cost`. The condition is now `weight_kg <= 1`.
- **Checked:** `shipping_cost(1) == 500`, `shipping_cost(1.01) == 900`, and `shipping_cost(0.4) == 500`.

## Issue #7: Free shipping for orders over $50
- **Decision:** enhancement. This is a request for new behavior. `shipping_cost` takes only a weight,
  and its docstring defines no order total, so nothing in the spec supports this yet.
- **Changed:** nothing. The feature needs an order-total parameter and a docstring change, which the
  maintainer should decide on.

## Issue #8: Median on the sales dashboard is wrong for an even number of days
- **Decision:** bug. The docstring says the median of an even count is the average of the two middle
  values. The code returned only the upper middle value.
- **Changed:** `huskyutils/stats.py`, `median`. An odd count returns the middle value. An even count
  returns the average of the two middle values, which is a float (for example `25.0`).
- **Checked:** `median([10,20,30,40]) == 25.0`, `median([4,1,3,2]) == 2.5`, `median([3,1,2]) == 2`,
  `median([7]) == 7`.

## Issue #9: 5 kg package should be in the heavy tier
- **Decision:** not_a_bug. The docstring says "Over 1 kg, up to and including 5 kg: $9.00" and "Over 5 kg:
  $9.00 plus $2.00". A 5 kg package is therefore $9.00 under the spec, and the code matches. The reporter
  wants $11.00, which would be a change to the shipping table. That needs a docstring change and a
  decision from the business, not a code fix.
- **Changed:** nothing.
- **Checked:** `shipping_cost(5) == 900`, as the docstring says.

## Issue #10: Product card description runs past the edge of the card
- **Decision:** bug. The code cut the text at `limit` characters and then appended "...", so the result
  could be `limit + 3` long. The docstring requires at most `limit` characters, whole words only, and

  The existing truncate tests still pass.

- Bugs fixed: #1, #2, #4, #5, #6, #8, #10. Changed files: `text.py`, `money.py`, `dates.py`,

    if days == 0:
        return start
    result = start
    counted = 0
    while counted < days:
        result += timedelta(days=1)
        if result.weekday() < 5 and result not in holidays:
            counted += 1
    return result

"""Delivery time windows."""


def merge_intervals(intervals):
    """Merge overlapping delivery windows.

    `intervals` is a list of [start, end] pairs with start <= end, in any order. Windows that
    overlap or touch (one ends where the next starts) are merged into one. The result is sorted by
    start time.

    Returns a new list. The input list and the pairs in it are not modified.

        merge_intervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10]]) == [[1, 6], [8, 10]]
        merge_intervals([[1, 4], [4, 5]]) == [[1, 5]]
    """
    merged = []
    for start, end in sorted(intervals):
        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])
    return merged

"""Payments."""


def split_amount(cents, people):
    """Split an amount in cents into `people` shares, for a shared order.

    The shares add up to exactly `cents` and differ by at most one cent. When the amount does not
    divide evenly, the first shares get the extra cent. A negative amount (a refund) is split the
    same way as the positive amount, with every share negative. `people` is at least 1.

        split_amount(900, 3) == [300, 300, 300]
        split_amount(1000, 3) == [334, 333, 333]
        split_amount(-1000, 3) == [-334, -333, -333]
    """
    if cents < 0:
        return [-share for share in split_amount(-cents, people)]
    base, extra = divmod(cents, people)
    return [base + 1] * extra + [base] * (people - extra)

"""Shipping prices."""
import math


def shipping_cost(weight_kg):
    """The shipping price of a package, in cents.

    - Up to and including 1 kg: $5.00
    - Over 1 kg, up to and including 5 kg: $9.00
    - Over 5 kg: $9.00 plus $2.00 for each started kilogram over 5

        shipping_cost(0.4) == 500
        shipping_cost(5.2) == 1100
    """
    if weight_kg <= 1:
        return 500
    if weight_kg <= 5:
        return 900
    return 900 + 200 * math.ceil(weight_kg - 5)

"""Statistics for the sales dashboard."""


def median(values):
    """The median of a non-empty list of numbers.

    The values can be in any order, and the list is not modified. With an odd number of values the
    median is the middle one. With an even number it is the average of the two middle values.

        median([3, 1, 2]) == 2
        median([4, 1, 3, 2]) == 2.5
    """
    ordered = sorted(values)
    mid = len(ordered) // 2
    if len(ordered) % 2:
        return ordered[mid]
    return (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2

"""Text helpers for product pages."""
import unicodedata


def slugify(title):
    """Turn a product title into a URL slug.

    The slug is lowercase ASCII. Accented letters lose their accents (é becomes e). Letters and
    digits are kept. Every run of other characters (spaces, punctuation, symbols) becomes a single
    hyphen, and the slug never starts or ends with a hyphen. A title with no letters or digits gives
    the empty string.

        slugify("Wireless Headphones") == "wireless-headphones"
        slugify("USB-C Dock (2nd gen)") == "usb-c-dock-2nd-gen"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Mug") == "creme-brulee-mug"
    """
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
    ascii_title = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii").lower()
    out = []
    for ch in ascii_title:
        if ch.isascii() and ch.isalnum():
            out.append(ch)
        elif out and out[-1] != "-":
            out.append("-")
    return "".join(out).strip("-")


def word_count(text):
    """Count the words in a review.

    Words are separated by whitespace. Punctuation stays attached to the word it touches, so
    "great," and "don't" are one word each.

        word_count("Great keyboard, fast shipping") == 4
    """
    return len(text.split())
